// purpose: Deno's configuration root for supabase/functions/**. It exists for a second reason beyond settings: WITHOUT a deno.json here, Deno walks up the tree looking for a workspace root, finds pnpm-workspace.yaml, and REWRITES the repo's root package.json to add a `workspaces` key. That file belongs to another stream. Anchoring Deno here stops the walk.
// imports: Import map. @supabase/supabase-js is pinned HERE, once (P2 #7, 2026-11-05): it used to be written as jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2.58.0 in 7 files, so a bump had 7 places to drift. Every file imports the bare name. Node never resolves it: the files node --test loads use `import type` only, which Node's type stripping erases, and the value importers (_shared/db/client.ts, rls-proof) are Deno-only. Note Node's worker pins supabase-js 2.50.0 separately (worker/package.json): the two runtimes still run different client versions. @applyy/shared-types stays a relative import (_shared/contracts/shared-types.ts) because node --test cannot read this map.
// compilerOptions: Kept aligned with the repo's tsconfig.base.json. Deno does not read that file, so the strictness settings that matter for the anti-fabrication work are restated rather than assumed.

compilerOptions.// noUncheckedIndexedAccess: Load-bearing for PROJECT_PLAN.md §10: an index into the master profile that may not exist is typed as possibly-undefined, which is the check the validator relies on.

// exclude: Test files are excluded from `deno check` because they import node:test, which pulls Node type-reference directives Deno cannot resolve. They are run by `node --test` instead — the pure functions are runtime-agnostic by design, so the runtime that executes the tests need not be the runtime that ships them. RENAMED 2026-09-10 from *_test.ts to *.test.ts: the Deno convention advertised a Deno runner that this very exclude rules out, and `deno test` reported 'No test modules found'. The name now matches the runner that actually runs them. These globs are COUPLED to that name — change one and the other must follow, or deno check silently resumes checking files it cannot resolve.
// lint: Default rules are fine; the recommended set already covers the mistakes that matter here.
